title: Credit River Watershed and Region of Peel Natural Areas Inventory - with all NAI
description:
Natural Areas Inventories are designed to provide biological and ecological information that can be used to establish baseline conditions on natural heritage features and functions present at varying geographic scales, including at a project site, for an area or over a municipality or a watershed.

A link to the Credit River Watershed and Region of Peel NAI Report – Volume 1 can be found Here.

INSTRUCTIONS

Use the Zoom + or Zoom - buttons (or hold shift and drag a box) to navigate to a Natural Area with Site Summary outlined in red. If multiple selections occur, press the white Next feature arrow in the top right of the pop-up window until Link to Site Summary (PDF) is found. Click on More info from the pop-up window to view the Site Summary.

For a list of all plants growing naturally in the study area, click Here.

For a list of the animals (birds, fish, butterflies, dragonflies/damselflies, reptiles, amphibians and mammals) of the study area, click Here.

For descriptions of dominant plants in all of the plant communities of the study area, click Here.

For background information on the project and on the study area (geology, physiography, soils, hydrology, human history, natural heritage and environmental management) and a description of the sections of the site summaries, click Here.

Additional details are available on a need-to-know basis by submitting a Data Request to the appropriate Conservation Authority. Email contact details are available for each Natural Area with Site Summary on the interactive map.

Requests for data on other natural areas in the Credit River watershed should be directed to CVC (Jacquelyn Kiers:
jkiers@creditvalleyca.ca). Requests for data on other natural areas in the Etobicoke Creek watershed, Mimico Creek watershed and Humber River watershed portions of the Region of Peel should be directed to TRCA (Susan Hayes: SHayes@trca.on.ca).

This map is intended for illustration purposes only. The information shown should not be interpreted to represent the most up-to-date or accurate surveyed information.
snippet: A Natural Areas Inventory (NAI) is an inventory of the biological resources of a natural area – it documents the species and ecological features that are present in an area.
